searchDocs.title: Configuration rules​
searchDocs.content: Use stable string identifiers for persisted or networked entities.Keep server-sensitive decisions server-side even when display config is replicated.Reference assets by configured name or object; do not scatter magic IDs.Avoid starting loops, connecting events, or mutating player state while a config module is required.Validate config at service startup and fail with the exact missing key.Reuse a definition instead of duplicating it in a controller.

searchDocs.title: Sound config structure​
searchDocs.content: Shared.Sounds exposes:  Field	ContentsIds	Named UI, ambience, music, gameplay, and footstep asset IDs Areas	Area playlists and transition settings Defaults	Shared playback defaults SoundGroups	Master, SFX, music, and merchant groups Sources	SoundHandler one-shot and loop source definitions

searchDocs.title: Store configuration​
searchDocs.content: Catalog entries are consumed by both presentation and authoritative services. Keep client-visible information harmless; the server re-resolves the selected entry and controls price, grant, and ownership.

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: Settings identifiers must match saved keys in DefaultData.Settings unless a control is explicitly session-only. ReplayFirstTimeChallenge, for example, is a command-style setting and is not persisted like a normal preference.

searchDocs.title: Adding configuration​
searchDocs.content: Choose a stable module and key.Document its consumer and authority.Add defaults or migration behavior for saved values.Validate malformed and missing values.Update this reference and the owning system guide.

searchDocs.title: Mince ByteNet addon
searchDocs.content: Mince ByteNet addon The ByteNet addon adds typed, buffer-backed packets alongside Mince's existing remotes. Use packets for frequent, predictable payloads. Keep ordinary remotes for infrequent or highly variable messages. Define each namespace in one shared ModuleScript that both the server and client require: local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Mince = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.Mince) return Mince:DefinePackets("Observatory", function(Net) return { ScooterSpeed = { Value = Net.struct({ rotationSpeed = Net.float32, }), Reliability = "unreliable", }, FishSnapshot = { Value = Net.struct({ id = Net.uint16, position = Net.vec3, velocity = Net.vec3, }), Reliability = "unreliable", }, } end) Server usage: local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.NetworkPackets) Packets.FishSnapshot.sendTo({ id = fishId, position = position, velocity = velocity, }, player) Client usage: local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.NetworkPackets) Packets.FishSnapshot.listen(function(snapshot) -- Apply the snapshot locally. end) Use unreliable for replaceable updates such as poses, velocity, and steering. Use reliable for inventory, purchases, rewards, state transitions, and any message that must arrive in order. Validate every client packet on the server; serialization does not provide security.

searchDocs.title: Static and event creatures​
searchDocs.content: Models tagged ServerCreatures are registered byCreatureAnimationService. The service records a server-time epoch and speed, then sends snapshots through CreatureAnimationPackets.  CreatureAnimationController:  loads the model's valid Animation,supports Humanoid and AnimationController rigs,starts playback at the server-relative time,corrects drift periodically,respects forced loop behavior for finite phenomena,cleans tracks when tags or models disappear.  The visible cosmetic track is client-owned. A phenomenon may use a zero-weight server timing track to count authored animation loops and schedule despawn without competing for the visible pose.

searchDocs.title: Boid schools​
searchDocs.content: FishNode / Boid tag | v FishController distance tracking | v FishBrain school lifecycle | v FishBehaviour simulation + interpolation ^ | BoidPackets target batches from server   FishController tracks school nodes, activates nearby schools, stops inactive ones, and owns the shared stepping decision.  FishBrain clones the configured fish model, chooses safe spawn positions, creates school members, registers animation tracks, and supports start, stop, resume, and destruction.  FishBehaviour contains schooling, steering, target following, obstacle avoidance, visual interpolation, animation-speed adjustment, and device-aware performance behavior. It exposes registration functions and performance metrics for shared scheduling.

searchDocs.title: Performance ownership​
searchDocs.content: Do not create one render or physics connection per creature.Cache animators and tracks instead of scanning descendants in hot paths.Stop simulation and interpolation for dormant schools.Use distance hysteresis to prevent rapid activation thrashing.Remove fish from global registries before destroying models.Treat invalid vectors, non-finite speeds, and missing targets defensively.  The detailed rollout checklist lives inCreature animation LOD plan.

searchDocs.title: Adding a school​
searchDocs.content: Create the fish asset with a valid pivot, animation, and collision setup.Add the expected boid/spawn configuration.Tag the world node correctly.Verify safe spawn bounds and obstacle behavior.Test activation, dormancy, resume, and streaming.Inspect animation-track and connection counts after repeated cycles.

searchDocs.title: Adding a placed creature​
searchDocs.content: Use the ServerCreatures tag.Include one valid animation source.Set AnimationSpeed only when the authored speed needs an override.Keep gameplay markers explicit and limited.Confirm late-joining clients receive the snapshot.Confirm removing and re-adding the tag does not duplicate tracks.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: Reduce client animation, skinning, and simulation CPU cost.Keep nearby creatures smooth and visually unchanged.Reduce update frequency for medium-distance creatures.Stop animation and simulation for distant creatures.Avoid creating a Heartbeat, RenderStepped, or PreSimulation connection per creature or school.Preserve creature events, scanning, discovery, and exhibit interactions.

searchDocs.title: Current Baseline​
searchDocs.content: Observed place totals:  Approximately 266 instances tagged Creatures.Approximately 52 instances tagged Boid.Approximately 323 AnimationController instances.Approximately 3,116 bones and 4,705 mesh parts.  Relevant runtime paths:  ReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Source.Components.CreaturesServerScriptService.Runtime.Source.Components.ServerCreaturesReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Source.Components.FishComponentReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Source.Controllers.FishControllerReplicatedStorage.Modules.FishBrainReplicatedStorage.Modules.FishBehaviour  Known architectural issues:  The Creatures component immediately loads and plays every valid animation without distance or visibility checks.ServerCreatures also loads and plays animations, so ownership must be audited to prevent duplicate server/client animation work.Each fish school created by FishBrain owns a PreSimulation connection.FishBehaviour also has a global PreSimulation path, but the group registration API is not consistently used by FishBrain.Fish visual interpolation runs every rendered frame for all entries in VisualCFrameTargets.Animation speed adjustments can traverse descendants when cached tracks are unavailable.FishController already performs a 0.3-second octree distance query, making it the natural owner for activation state.

searchDocs.title: LOD Targets​
searchDocs.content: Initial values are intentionally conservative and should become configuration values after validation.  Tier	Distance	Animation	Simulation	Visual transformNear	0–75 studs	Full speed	30 Hz	Every rendered frame Medium	75–175 studs	Full track at reduced evaluation rate	10–15 Hz	Interpolated Far	175–250 studs	Paused or 4–6 Hz	4–6 Hz	Coarse interpolation Dormant	Beyond 250 studs	Stopped	Stopped	No updates

searchDocs.title: Phase 0 — Measurement and Safety Net​
searchDocs.content: Record client FPS with creature simulation enabled and disabled. Capture MicroProfiler samples at the observatory, aquarium, and open-water areas. Record Script Profiler time for Creatures, FishController, FishBrain, and FishBehaviour. Count active animation tracks by LOD tier. Count active fish, schools, and visual interpolation targets. Record client memory and CPU from an empty server after 60 seconds. Record the same values with at least one additional player. Add a temporary developer-only metrics API or attributes for active/dormant counts. Confirm scanning, discovery, animation markers, and creature events before changes. Save baseline screenshots or video for visual comparison.  Exit criteria:   Baseline numbers are recorded in this document or a linked results document. A repeatable playtest route exists.

searchDocs.title: Phase 1 — Static Creature Animation Manager​
searchDocs.content: Scope: instances tagged Creatures and ServerCreatures, excluding boid schools.   Create one client CreatureAnimationController responsible for animation activation decisions. Register/unregister creature components with the controller. Cache each creature's root part, animator, animation track, and event-marker connections once. Replace unconditional AnimationTrack:Play() with controller-owned activation. Evaluate creature distance from the camera or character on a shared 5 Hz scheduler task. Keep near creature tracks playing normally. Pause medium/far tracks without destroying and reloading them. Stop dormant tracks after a grace period to prevent rapid boundary thrashing. Add LOD hysteresis so a creature does not repeatedly start and stop near a boundary. Disconnect marker events when a component is removed. Remove debug prints from animation markers. Audit ServerCreatures and document which animations genuinely require server ownership. Remove duplicate server animation playback where animation is cosmetic-only. Preserve server-owned animation only when gameplay or replicated marker behavior requires it.  Exit criteria:   Nearby static creature animation looks unchanged. Distant static creature tracks stop consuming animation time. No duplicate track is created when crossing an LOD boundary repeatedly. Creature event emitters still fire exactly once when expected.  Rollback:   A configuration flag can restore unconditional animation playback.

searchDocs.title: Phase 2 — Fish School Activation Ownership​
searchDocs.content: Scope: FishComponent, FishController, and FishBrain lifecycle.   Make FishController the single owner of school activation and LOD selection. Replace the hardcoded local DesiredDrawDistance = 200 or ... expression with a real player setting fallback. Store tracked school positions in the octree and update nodes when regions move. Assign each school an explicit Near, Medium, Far, or Dormant state. Use separate enter/exit radii to prevent activation thrashing. Remove one PreSimulation connection per FishBrain instance. Register active fish groups with the existing global FishBehaviour.RegisterGroup path. Unregister groups on stop and destruction. Ensure dormant fish are not left in global interpolation or animation caches. Avoid reparenting every fish repeatedly when crossing a boundary; compare pausing versus dormant storage. Confirm stopped schools can resume without duplicating fish or animation tracks.  Exit criteria:   There is one shared fish simulation connection per client. Dormant schools perform no simulation or interpolation work. Repeated activation does not increase connections, fish count, or memory.  Rollback:   A feature flag can restore the existing FishBrain connection behavior.

searchDocs.title: Phase 3 — Simulation and Animation LOD​
searchDocs.content: Scope: active boids inside FishBehaviour.   Pass the school LOD tier into FishGroup:Step rather than calculating inconsistent tiers in multiple places. Near schools simulate at approximately 30 Hz. Medium schools simulate at 10–15 Hz. Far schools simulate at 4–6 Hz with reduced neighbor counts. Dormant schools do not call FishGroup:Step. Limit obstacle raycasts by tier. Limit leadership and school-center recalculation by tier. Cache animation tracks for every fish; remove descendant scans from hot paths. Adjust animation speed only when the delta exceeds the existing threshold. Pause fish animation tracks in the dormant tier. Resume tracks without calling LoadAnimation again. Bound the global CFrame queue and carry excess work into the next frame. Remove stale VisualCFrameTargets immediately when fish become dormant. Interpolate only near and medium fish every rendered frame. Use coarse direct transforms for far fish.  Exit criteria:   Frame time remains stable when entering an area with several schools. Simulation work scales with nearby fish rather than total fish in the place. No visible teleporting occurs at the near/medium boundary. Far fish remain visually acceptable at the target camera distance.

searchDocs.title: Phase 4 — Adaptive Quality and Streaming​
searchDocs.content: Move LOD distances and update rates into shared configuration. Define desktop, console, and mobile presets. Base adaptive quality on a rolling frame-time average, not a single frame. Degrade one tier at a time after sustained low FPS. Recover quality slowly after sustained healthy FPS. Respect the player's draw-distance setting. Verify behavior with Workspace.StreamingEnabled on and off. Handle streamed-out creatures as unregister events without warnings. Avoid loading animation tracks until the creature is eligible for an active tier. Add a maximum number of simultaneously animated skinned creatures per device preset.  Exit criteria:   Mobile and low-performance clients automatically reduce creature cost. Quality recovery does not cause frame-time spikes. Streaming in/out does not leak tracks, connections, or component state.

searchDocs.title: Phase 5 — Validation and Rollout​
searchDocs.content: Repeat the Phase 0 playtest route. Compare CPU, FPS, frame time, memory, and active track counts against baseline. Test all creature event-marker effects. Test scanning and discovery on near, far, stopped, and resumed creatures. Test player teleportation between areas to force rapid LOD changes. Test two clients observing the same creatures from different distances. Test Studio, desktop client, mobile emulation, and console emulation. Run for at least 20 minutes and check for connection or memory growth. Remove temporary diagnostic output. Keep metrics accessible behind a developer flag. Roll out behind a feature flag before making it the default. Record final measurements and mark the selected default thresholds.

searchDocs.title: Success Criteria​
searchDocs.content: At least a 30% reduction in creature-related client script time in the heavy test area. No more than 10% of total creature tracks active while the player is far from exhibits and schools. No per-creature or per-school frame connection for activation decisions. Stable connection and memory counts after repeated LOD transitions. No regression in scanning, discovery, creature events, or nearby visual quality.

searchDocs.title: Mince remotes​
searchDocs.content: Mince:GetEvent(name) creates or resolves a remote namespace.event:Extend(name) creates a named channel beneath it. Remote functions useMince:GetFunction.  Major namespaces include:  Namespace	PurposeStoreEvents	Purchase, equip, unequip, gift, inventory, and gear-stat messages Achievements	Progress updates, claims, and toast presentation Phenomena	Timeline and registry snapshots DiscoverySystem	Discovery recording and discovery list requests OxygenEvents	Authoritative oxygen snapshots Tipjar	Listings, donation prompts, visibility, results, and activity Jukebox	Track requests, selection, playback, shuffle, and genre TreasureEvent	Open results and collected-state synchronization GearVisibilityEvents	Player preference requests for diving gear AnalyticsFunnel	Onboarding step reporting  Names are contracts. A spelling change must update both server and every client consumer in the same change.

searchDocs.title: ByteNet​
searchDocs.content: Mince's ByteNet addon registers one shared schema function per namespace and asserts that repeated definitions agree. Packet modules belong inReplicatedStorage.Modules.  Current first-party packet groups:  Module	Namespace	UseBoidPackets	Boids	Batched simulation targets and client readiness CreatureAnimationPackets	CreatureAnimations	Synchronized creature animation snapshots RealismPackets	Realism	Character look/pose replication  return Mince:DefinePackets("Feature", function(Net) return { Update = { Value = Net.struct({ id = Net.string, value = Net.float32, }), Reliability = "unreliable", }, } end)   Use reliable packets for state transitions that cannot be dropped. Use unreliable packets only for replaceable, frequently refreshed state such as poses or simulation targets.

searchDocs.title: Validation boundary​
searchDocs.content: Every client-to-server request must validate:  the sending player and current character,requested identifiers against server-owned configuration,ownership, balance, cooldown, and distance requirements,numeric finiteness and acceptable ranges,the current state transition.  Never trust a client-provided price, reward, entitlement, target player object, or inventory record.

searchDocs.title: Snapshot pattern​
searchDocs.content: Systems such as creature animation and phenomena keep authoritative registries on the server. A client sends a ready/request signal, receives a full snapshot, then consumes incremental updates. This prevents initialization order from silently losing state that existed before the controller connected.

searchDocs.title: System map​
searchDocs.content: Roblox place and tagged instances | v Mince loaders | +--------+---------+ | | v v Server runtime Client runtime services/data controllers/UI | | +--- remotes -------+ +--- ByteNet -------+ | v Profile data, discoveries, creatures, economy, store, phenomena, and world UI

searchDocs.title: Where to begin​
searchDocs.content: Goal	GuideUnderstand boot and module discovery	Runtime lifecycle Add or change a network message	Networking Work on saves, currency, or achievements	Player data and economy Change scanning or the encyclopedia	Discovery and scanning Work on fish, static creatures, or animation	Creature systems Add a scheduled creature appearance	Phenomena and events Change swimming, oxygen, or underwater visuals	Movement and environment Add store inventory or purchase behavior	Commerce and inventory Change UI, notifications, or sound	Interface and audio Add a tagged object to the place	World components

searchDocs.title: Source boundaries​
searchDocs.content: ServerScriptService/Runtime owns authoritative data and gameplay decisions.ReplicatedStorage/Runtime owns shared configuration and client runtime code.ReplicatedStorage/Modules contains Mince, networking schemas, UI modules, simulation libraries, and reusable utilities.ReplicatedStorage/Assets contains discoverable species definitions and runtime assets.ServerStorage/Runtime contains the separate LightRunner boot path and server-only implementation assets.  Third-party packages and Roblox's default player modules are dependencies, not first-party extension points. Avoid editing them unless the dependency itself is intentionally being forked.

searchDocs.title: Engineering rules​
searchDocs.content: The server owns profile data, currency, entitlements, rewards, and grants.Client requests must be validated against server configuration and state.A tagged component must clean up every connection, animation track, and transient instance it creates.ByteNet packet schemas live in replicated modules and are shared verbatim by both sides.Sound asset IDs belong only in the shared sound configuration.Run StyLua and Selene on touched Luau, then build Moonwave before publishing.

searchDocs.title: Swimming​
searchDocs.content: SwimmingService owns server character setup and the Swim remote contract.SwimmingController owns responsive local movement:  camera-relative horizontal movement,ascent and descent input,buoyancy and drag,physics constraints and orientation,directional swimming animations,character IK,equipped DPV speed modifiers,gamepad and mobile input,character lifecycle cleanup.  The client computes responsive forces, while the server controls which characters may enter or leave the swimming state.

searchDocs.title: Oxygen​
searchDocs.content: OxygenService attaches authoritative oxygen state to characters and sendsOxygenEvents.OxygenSync updates. It disables conflicting default health scripts where required and applies depletion or recovery based on the character's environment.  OxygenBalance renders the player's oxygen. DepthAtmosphereControllerconsumes the same state to coordinate environmental presentation.  Do not let a UI bar or local attribute become the authoritative oxygen value.

searchDocs.title: Underwater presentation​
searchDocs.content: System	ResponsibilityDepthAtmosphereController	Depth-sensitive atmosphere and oxygen presentation UnderwaterVisionController	Vision behavior influenced by owned/equipped gear Caustics component	Tagged underwater light texture animation AreaController	Area-specific music playlists and transitions SoundHandler	Sound groups, sources, loops, and music overrides Realism_Controller	Head/character pose replication and material footsteps

searchDocs.title: Vehicles and equipment​
searchDocs.content: DPVService validates and configures double-DPV state on the server.DoubleDPV handles client animation, motor presentation, and registration.ScooterService and the Scooter component provide the corresponding single-vehicle contract.  Gear visibility is split between authoritative attachment behavior and a player setting synchronized through GearVisibilityEvents.

searchDocs.title: Character cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Movement systems attach constraints, IK controls, animation tracks, input bindings, render callbacks, and tool listeners. Cleanup must run on:  character removal,humanoid death,swimming disable,tool unequip,controller destruction,teleport or state replacement.  Repeated character spawns are the primary leak test for this subsystem.

searchDocs.title: Cross-device testing​
searchDocs.content: Test keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch controls, VR, and mobile emulation. Verify simultaneous directional and vertical input, camera-relative movement, DPV transitions, oxygen depletion, and the absence of orphaned mobile buttons.

searchDocs.title: Inspect, edit, validate, sync​
searchDocs.content: Inspect live Studio path | v Pull the exact script | v Edit mapped local source | v StyLua + Selene + relevant tests | v Push that file once | v Confirm Abraxius status is live   Do not retry a push reported as pending. Abraxius tracks it until Studio confirms the source.

searchDocs.title: Local commands​
searchDocs.content: npm run format npm run quality npm run docs:build npm run docs:serve   The repository contains legacy and vendored source with existing warnings. During focused changes, run StyLua and Selene on every touched first-party file and report unrelated baseline failures separately.

searchDocs.title: Documentation standards​
searchDocs.content: Write task-oriented pages with ownership and data flow.Use exact module names and stable identifiers.Explain server authority and cleanup requirements.Prefer diagrams and tables only where they clarify relationships.Link related systems instead of duplicating long explanations.Run Moonwave with broken-link checking set to throw.

searchDocs.title: Publishing​
searchDocs.content: Moonwave builds the static site with a base path of /observatory/. The portfolio repository copies the generated site under public/observatory, and its Vite GitHub Pages build publishes that folder unchanged.  Observatory docs + selected source annotations | v moonwave build | v portfolio/public/observatory | v npm run build:pages | v velumix.github.io/observatory/

searchDocs.title: Change checklist​
searchDocs.content: Inspect the live implementation before documenting behavior.Keep private credentials, secrets, and operational endpoints out of public documentation.Update the module map when ownership moves.Update saved-data docs when schema changes.Update networking docs when a remote or packet contract changes.Verify the published subpath locally before pushing the website.

searchDocs.title: UI layers​
searchDocs.content: Layer	ExamplesFoundation	UIFactory, UIColors, InterfaceHandler, buttons, sliders, card stacks, push/pop Screen components	Store, achievements, encyclopedia, settings, tip jar, elevator, jukebox HUD components	Currency, health, oxygen, directional markers, notifications Controllers	UserInterface, StoreController, TopbarManager, TooltipController World displays	GlobalEventDisplay, exhibit UI, popups, markers  Premade StarterGui templates should own stable layout and script-facing names. Runtime modules populate content, clone small templates, and bind behavior.

searchDocs.title: Navigation​
searchDocs.content: InterfaceHandler coordinates screen configuration, visibility transitions, button behavior, and stacked navigation. Screens should close through the handler rather than mutating unrelated GUI visibility directly.  Camera-owning screens must coordinate with CameraControlManager and release ownership on every close path.

searchDocs.title: Notifications​
searchDocs.content: There are two presentation paths:  notices for general server messages,typed notification cards for information, success, warning, and error.  The ShowNotifications player setting must be respected without preventing the underlying gameplay result.

searchDocs.title: Audio authority​
searchDocs.content: Runtime.Config.Shared.Sounds is the only first-party location for sound asset IDs. It contains:  UI interaction and notification IDs,ambience,area playlists,intro, open-ocean, and merchant music,gameplay SFX,material footsteps,sound groups and SoundHandler source definitions.  SoundHandler owns source creation, one-shots, positioned playback, loops, stack arbitration, group volume, and music overrides. UIAudio is a playback adapter and contains no IDs.  warning Do not add an asset ID to a controller, component, or UI module. Add it to the shared sound config and reference the named entry.

searchDocs.title: Area music​
searchDocs.content: AreaController consumes Sounds.Areas, builds Sound objects, and responds to the player's tagged area. Area settings define volume, fade time, crossfade, order, looping, and priority.  Merchant playback uses a separate sound group so it can remain audible while the normal music group is ducked.

searchDocs.title: UI quality checklist​
searchDocs.content: Semantic instance names and stable lookup paths.Templates hidden or detached during runtime.Input parity for mouse, touch, gamepad, and VR.No connections or camera state left behind after close.Sound volume routed through the correct group.Hover and click feedback do not fire for disabled controls.Notification dots expose explicit enabled state and stop pulsing when clear.

searchDocs.title: Boot sequence​
searchDocs.content: The server loader requires ReplicatedStorage.Modules.Mince.Replicated and server configuration folders are loaded into Mince.Config.Server runtime modules are discovered recursively.Mince:Start() runs lifecycle work and establishes the server handshake.The client-context loader waits for the server setup identity.The client loads replicated configuration and replicated runtime modules.The client calls Mince:Start().  The handshake prevents client controllers from assuming the authoritative runtime exists before server startup completes.

searchDocs.title: A service module​
searchDocs.content: local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Mince = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.Mince) local ExampleService = { Name = "ExampleService", } function ExampleService:Setup() self.Remote = Mince:GetEvent("Example") end function ExampleService:GameStart() -- Begin work only after runtime setup. end return ExampleService   Keep module top-level code limited to dependency lookup and immutable definitions. Connections, loops, and world mutations belong in lifecycle methods so startup order remains observable.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: Mince.Component { Tag = "Example" } connects behavior to CollectionService tags. A component typically implements:  Method	UseConstruct	Cache instance references and initialize per-instance state Start	Begin behavior after construction Stop or cleanup hook	Disconnect listeners and release transient objects  Components are registered by instance and can be retrieved through the component registry. Parent validation prevents components from mounting in invalid hierarchies.

searchDocs.title: Discovery rules​
searchDocs.content: Mince recursively examines configured source folders, but nested ModuleScripts inside another ModuleScript act as private children. This is whyRealism_Controller.Config and ScanController.TargetManager are required by their parents rather than registered as independent controllers.

searchDocs.title: Failure behavior​
searchDocs.content: The runtime's safe require path can keep startup moving after a module require failure. That is useful for availability, but it makes Studio output and targeted testing essential: a failed module can appear as an empty table until a dependent feature accesses it.  warning Never use safe-require tolerance as validation. A clean startup must have no new require warnings, and every changed module must pass Selene and parse checks.

searchDocs.title: Adding a module​
searchDocs.content: Choose the authoritative runtime band.Give the table a unique Name.Keep dependencies available on that side of the client/server boundary.Create remotes or packet schemas in replicated code.Put connections in Setup and active loops in GameStart.Make teardown explicit for components and character-bound behavior.Add the module to the module map.

searchDocs.title: Runtime bands​
searchDocs.content: Band	Location	ResponsibilityConfiguration	ReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Config	Store items, settings, sound, stats, input, passes, rarities, and shared definitions Server data	ServerScriptService.Runtime.Source.Data	Profile lifecycle, defaults, session counters, and replicated player state Server services	ServerScriptService.Runtime.Source.Services	Authoritative economy, purchases, gear, phenomena, oxygen, tools, analytics, and live systems Server systems	ServerScriptService.Runtime.Source.Systems	Discovery, encyclopedia, settings, and event scheduling Client controllers	ReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Source.Controllers	Input, cameras, scanning, swimming, fish, UI state, phenomena, and presentation Components	Both runtime trees	CollectionService-backed behavior attached to tagged place instances Shared modules	ReplicatedStorage.Modules	Mince, ByteNet, UI, simulation, utilities, and packet definitions

searchDocs.title: Lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: Mince-loaded tables can expose Setup and GameStart. Setup establishes dependencies, remotes, registries, and listeners. GameStart begins work that requires the runtime to be assembled, such as update loops, initial snapshots, and player-facing controllers.  Module identity comes from the table's Name field when present and otherwise from the ModuleScript name. Mince:Get("CurrencyService"), for example, resolves the registered service after discovery.  See Runtime lifecycle for loading rules and safe module patterns.

searchDocs.title: Authority flow​
searchDocs.content: Input or tagged instance | v Client controller/component | | validated request v Server service/system | +--> profile mutation +--> world mutation +--> analytics | | result/snapshot v Client state and interface   The client may predict movement and render cosmetic state, but it must not decide purchases, ownership, rewards, discovery persistence, or receipt outcomes.

searchDocs.title: Separate LightRunner path​
searchDocs.content: ServerStorage.Runtime.Boot starts LightRunner for modules held under the server-storage runtime. Treat this as a separate loader with its own discovery rules. Do not assume a LightRunner module is available through Mince:Getunless an explicit bridge exists.

searchDocs.title: Dependency policy​
searchDocs.content: First-party systems may depend on shared libraries in ReplicatedStorage. Server-only modules must not be required by clients. Nested helper modules inside a ModuleScript are private implementation details and are not automatically registered as top-level Mince services.

searchDocs.title: Server components​
searchDocs.content: Tag/module	ResponsibilityBeg	Reward interaction, streak behavior, effects, ragdoll, and toss Deadly	Damage from hazardous world models DoorServer	Authoritative door behavior FishNode	Server-side fish target or node registration Jukebox	Authoritative jukebox control and replication LiveNpc	NPC conversation state ServerCreatures	Server-side creature asset sanitation and ownership Trash	Environmental cleanup collection and reward request

searchDocs.title: Client components​
searchDocs.content: Tag/module	ResponsibilityBoid / FishComponent	Fish school configuration and lifecycle Creatures	Placed creature presentation Exhibit	Exhibit interaction, viewing, and discovery metadata Selectable	World target registration Interactable	Generic prompt-driven interactions Door	Door presentation Elevator	Elevator interaction, camera, and deep-sea preview DoubleDPV / Scooter	Vehicle presentation and control Jukebox	Local prompt and UI bridge Chair	Seated animation selection Caustics	Underwater texture animation EventDisplay	Phenomenon schedule display Marker	Directional marker UI Emitter	Tagged particle behavior Hatch	Swim transition Blender	Drink-making interaction ShopNpc / Npc	Merchant and conversation interaction

searchDocs.title: Component contract​
searchDocs.content: A component should:  validate the tagged instance class and required children,cache references during construction,bind behavior once,guard asynchronous callbacks against destruction,disconnect and destroy everything it owns,tolerate streaming removal and re-addition.

searchDocs.title: Authoring tags​
searchDocs.content: Tags are public configuration. Renaming a tag is a place migration, not a private refactor. Update every authored instance and both client/server consumers together.  Use attributes for small per-instance configuration such as IDs, display labels, area music keys, animation speed, or feature flags. Use shared config modules for reusable definitions and server-owned data for anything sensitive.

searchDocs.title: Testing​
searchDocs.content: For each component, test:  instance already present before startup,instance added after startup,instance streamed out or destroyed,tag removed and re-added,character death during interaction,repeated interaction without duplicated connections.

searchDocs.title: Profile lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: Player joins | v load ProfileService profile | v reconcile DefaultData | +--> LocalData registry +--> replicated state +--> DataSync snapshot | player leaves / shutdown | v run release callbacks -> release profile -> clean state   The manager exposes full profile access only on the server. UserProfile on the client receives full and partial synchronization events and should be treated as a presentation cache, not an authority.

searchDocs.title: Saved schema​
searchDocs.content: The default profile contains:  Root	DataSettings	Graphics, audio, caustics, notifications, head movement, debris, gear visibility, and tutorial state Statistics	Events, scans, exploration, playtime, currency, dives, trash, and minigames Currency	Balance, earned/spent totals, income timing, streaks, and source accounting EcoPoints	Environmental balance and source accounting Discoveries	Persisted discovery identifiers Achievements	Progress, unlock, and claim state OwnedItems	Ownership, equipped state, category, slot, and grant metadata CollectedTreasures	Daily or reset-bound treasure state Tipjar	Donation ledger and listing visibility AnalyticsTracking	Interface tracking records  When adding a field, update DefaultData and decide whether existing profiles can be reconciled safely or need an explicit migration keyed by __version.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: DataSync carries initial state. DataPartialSync updates a scoped portion of the client cache. Currency and eco-point balances also expose named Mince state objects for responsive UI.  Do not send internal ProfileService objects or server-only bookkeeping to the client.

searchDocs.title: CurrencyService​
searchDocs.content: CurrencyService owns mutations for the primary currency and Eco Points. Its public operations include grant, spend, balance lookup, trash collection, passive income, scan rewards, event rewards, and exploration rewards.  Each transaction:  resolves the active profile,validates amount and balance,updates totals and per-source accounting,synchronizes replicated state,reports economy analytics,sends a player-facing notification when appropriate.

searchDocs.title: Achievements and statistics​
searchDocs.content: AchievementService records stat progress, unlocks configured achievements, handles claims, and emits update/toast messages. Achievement definitions live in Runtime.Config.Shared.Achievements.  Statistics should be changed through their owning service so achievement progress and analytics remain consistent.

searchDocs.title: Safe mutation checklist​
searchDocs.content: Reject non-finite, negative, or unexpected amounts.Resolve item prices from server configuration.Keep receipt processing idempotent.Update saved totals and current balance together.Synchronize only after the mutation succeeds.Register release callbacks for any service holding per-player state.Test join, rejoin, forced save, leave, and shutdown paths.

searchDocs.title: Phenomenon definitions​
searchDocs.content: Definition modules under Systems.EventManager.Events provide:  stable identifier and display name,rarity and description,creature asset and scan ID,animation loop count,spawn offset or preserved position behavior,start and finish messages,despawn delay.  PhenomenonService loads the definitions into rarity pools and generates a rolling timeline from configured slot duration, slots per hour, rarity rules, and look-ahead hours.

searchDocs.title: Manifestation flow​
searchDocs.content: definition registry | v rolling timeline and slots | v compatible EventCreatureSpawn point | v clone EventAnimals asset | +--> ServerCreatures animation sync +--> scanner _fishId +--> notice and analytics | v finite loop timing -> fade -> destroy   Spawned models live under Workspace.GlobalEventCreatures. Event assets are tagged for creature animation tracking so every client receives synchronized playback.

searchDocs.title: Client presentation​
searchDocs.content: PhenomenonController requests timeline and registry snapshots from thePhenomena remote namespace. GlobalEventDisplay renders the schedule and current manifestation on tagged world displays. Player notices announce start and finish messages.  The service broadcasts timeline changes rather than making every client reconstruct server scheduling independently.

searchDocs.title: Adding a phenomenon​
searchDocs.content: Add the event creature asset to the configured asset folder.Give it the ServerCreatures tag and a valid animation.Add a definition module with a stable ID and scan ID.Choose UseSpawnPoints or PreservePosition deliberately.Set the finite animation loop count.Verify the asset matches at least one tracked spawn point.Test timeline display, manifestation, scanning, late join, fade, and cleanup.

searchDocs.title: Legacy EventManager​
searchDocs.content: EventManager can select, trigger, time, jump, and end generic event modules. It also owns EventInteract and EventToggle communication. Keep it for features that need that contract, but avoid registering the same creature appearance in both schedulers.

searchDocs.title: Failure handling​
searchDocs.content: Missing assets, invalid animations, and unavailable spawn points must fail the manifestation without leaving a timeline slot permanently active. Retry timing is tracked separately from manifested slots to avoid tight retry loops.

searchDocs.title: Runtime Flow​
searchDocs.content: Server boot starts in ServerScriptService/Runtime/MinceLoader.server.luau:  Load replicated config from ReplicatedStorage.Runtime.Config.Load server config from ServerScriptService.Runtime.Config.Recursively require eligible modules below ServerScriptService.Runtime.Source.Register module Setup and GameStart lifecycle methods.Run Mince:Start().  Mince provides four important framework surfaces:  Mince:Get(name) for module lookup.Mince:GetEvent(name) for remote events and named extensions.Mince:GetFunction(name) for remote functions with middleware.Mince:GetState(name) for server-owned replicated state.Mince.Component({ Tag = "..." }) for CollectionService-tagged components.  The intended architecture is service/controller modules with explicit Setup and GameStart phases, Mince-managed remotes, Mince-managed state for replicated values, and components for tagged world instances.

searchDocs.title: 1. Profile Data Has Too Many Writers​
searchDocs.content: Many services call PlayerDataManager:GetProfileData() or GetProfile() and mutate profile tables directly. Examples:  StoreService edits profile.Data.Currency, profile.Data.EcoPoints, profile.Data.OwnedItems, profile.Data.Statistics, and profile.Data.GearStats.PurchaseService edits PurchaseStats, PurchaseHistory, Gamepasses, and has a fallback path that directly increments currency.ToolService, DefaultGearService, TipjarService, AchievementService, DiscoverySystem, TreasureService, Statistics, and Settings also mutate profile sections.  This makes persistence and replication fragile because every caller must remember to call UpdatePlayer or SchedulePlayerUpdate for the right section. It also makes validation inconsistent.  Recommended direction:  Keep PlayerDataManager as the persistence owner.Add section-specific writer APIs instead of exposing raw profile tables for writes: PlayerDataManager:Patch(player, section, patchFn)PlayerDataManager:GetSection(player, section)PlayerDataManager:MarkDirty(player, section) Move economy writes behind CurrencyService.Move inventory writes behind an InventoryService or OwnershipService.Move profile stats writes behind Statistics.

searchDocs.title: 2. StoreService Bypasses CurrencyService Spending​
searchDocs.content: StoreService:HandlePurchase subtracts balances directly:  profile.Data.EcoPoints.Balance = ecoBalance - priceprofile.Data.Currency.Balance = balance - price  That bypasses CurrencyService:SpendCurrency, duplicated analytics logging, state sync, and future validation. It also has no matching SpendEcoPoints API.  Recommended direction:  Add CurrencyService:SpendEcoPoints(player, amount, source).Change StoreService purchases to call CurrencyService:SpendCurrency or SpendEcoPoints.Let CurrencyService own balance mutation, total spent, state sync, and analytics.StoreService should only own item validation and inventory grant/equip flow.

searchDocs.title: 3. PurchaseService Bypasses Mince RemoteFunction​
searchDocs.content: PurchaseService:Setup creates a raw RemoteFunction named PurchasePrompt under ReplicatedStorage.  That bypasses Mince:GetFunction, so it does not use the framework remote registry or middleware surface.  Recommended direction:  Replace the raw RemoteFunction with: local PurchasePrompt = Mince:GetFunction("PurchasePrompt")PurchasePrompt.OnInvoke = function(player, purchaseType, id) ... endoptional middleware for type checks and rate limits. Move product/gamepass prompt validation into small methods that are easy to test.

searchDocs.title: 4. Mince Lifecycle Ordering Is Only Partial​
searchDocs.content: Mince:Start() sorts SetupMethods and PostMethods, but then starts each setup with task.spawn. That means lower LoadOrder setup starts first, but it does not necessarily complete before higher-order setup starts.  Modules currently compensate by calling Mince:Get at top level or inside setup, but this can return proxy tables for modules that are not loaded yet.  Recommended direction:  Define lifecycle rules clearly: Setup should only connect remotes/events and initialize local state.GameStart should perform work that requires other modules to be ready. For modules with hard dependencies, use a sequential setup group or explicit dependency metadata: Dependencies = { "PlayerDataManager", "CurrencyService" }Mince waits for dependency setup completion before invoking the module. At minimum, document that LoadOrder controls start order, not completion order.

searchDocs.title: 5. Mince Safe Require Can Hide Broken Modules​
searchDocs.content: Mince.DoPcalling = true causes require failures to become empty module tables. This keeps the server alive but shifts failures to later runtime behavior.  Recommended direction:  Keep pcall in production only if needed, but record failed modules in Mince.FailedModules.During Studio or development, fail fast or expose a hard warning summary after load.Do not register empty tables as valid modules unless the caller explicitly opts in.

searchDocs.title: 6. Component Addon Depends On _G.MinceRef​
searchDocs.content: Mince/Addons/component.luau uses _G.MinceRef, and the file itself has a TODO: rewrite. This makes the component addon order-dependent and harder to isolate.  Recommended direction:  Pass the Mince instance into addon initialization instead of reading _G.Normalize component method names: current code calls Construct, but removal code looks for Removing/Destroying; some project components use Stop, which Mince does not call directly.Add a small component lifecycle adapter: ConstructStartStopDestroy

searchDocs.title: 1. Remote Event Extensions Are Useful But Under-Validated​
searchDocs.content: Extended events like StoreEvents:Extend("PurchaseRequest") and DrinkService:Extend("DrinkMade") help group feature traffic. The server remote addon also kicks players if they fire an unknown extension.  The current risk is that payload validation sits in each service method, if it exists at all.  Recommended direction:  Add optional middleware to Mince:GetEvent, similar to GetFunction.Define request schemas near each remote registration: Store purchase: player, category: string, itemName: stringSettings save: player, settings: tableDrink request: player, method: string, ... Prefer named function remotes for request/response traffic instead of custom "Response" packets on events.

searchDocs.title: 2. State Replication Is Underused​
searchDocs.content: Currency and EcoPoints now use Mince:GetState, but much of the client still receives whole profile chunks through DataSync and DataPartialSync.  Good candidates for Mince state:  Player economy: already partly done.Settings: player-owned state with registered set handlers.Inventory summary: owned/equipped state, read-only to client except through StoreService requests.Gear stats: GearStats_{UserId} instead of manual GearStatsUpdate event.Discovery progress: read-only state plus server request to record discoveries.  Recommended direction:  Use state for durable UI-facing values that change over time.Use events for transient effects/notifications.Use functions for request/response actions.

searchDocs.title: 3. Feature Boundaries Are Blurred​
searchDocs.content: Examples:  StoreService owns item validation, balance spending, stats, gear stat calculation, character attributes, kit/cosmetic application, asset ownership sync, and inventory sync.DrinkService owns components, recipes, cup state, ingredient rules, visuals, placement, trash logic, and client request routing.TipjarService owns profile persistence, HTTP/Roblox API calls, product listing cache, rate limiting, prompts, transfers, and ledger sync.ScanController owns input, camera, cursor, target selection, skeleton UI, effects, discovery events, and sound.BackpackController/Main/init.luau and Utility.luau are each over 2,000 lines.  Recommended direction:  Split by ownership, not by folder size alone.Keep public Mince module APIs small and delegate internals to private child ModuleScripts.Do not let child private modules be auto-loaded by Mince; the current loader already skips ModuleScripts under ModuleScripts, which is useful for this.

searchDocs.title: Economy And Store​
searchDocs.content: Create or clarify:  CurrencyService Owns Credits/EcoPoints mutation, state sync, economy analytics.Exposes GiveCurrency, SpendCurrency, GiveEcoPoints, SpendEcoPoints. InventoryService Owns OwnedItems, grants, ownership checks, equip flags.Exposes OwnsItem, GrantItem, EquipItem, UnequipItem. GearStatsService Calculates gear stats from equipped items.Applies character attributes and speed bases. StoreService Owns remote request routing and store-specific validation.Calls CurrencyService, InventoryService, GearStatsService, KitService.

searchDocs.title: Purchases​
searchDocs.content: Create or clarify:  PurchaseService Owns Marketplace callbacks and receipt idempotency.Uses Mince:GetFunction("PurchasePrompt"). EntitlementService Owns gamepass lookup, player attributes, ownership sync. ProductGrantService Maps developer products to grant handlers.

searchDocs.title: Player Data​
searchDocs.content: Keep:  PlayerDataManager Loads profiles, releases profiles, provides patch/dirty APIs, creates initial per-player Mince state.  Move out:  Section-specific mutation knowledge.Economy mutation.Item mutation.Achievement/stat business logic.

searchDocs.title: Drink System​
searchDocs.content: Split DrinkService/init.luau:  DrinkService/init.luau Mince module entry, remotes/functions, player cleanup. DrinkService/CupComponent.luau Server cup component and lifecycle. DrinkService/IngredientComponent.luau Ingredient rules. DrinkService/DrinkDomain.luau Pure recipe/mixing/name logic. DrinkService/DrinkPlacement.luau Placement and spawned drink handling.  Client:  DrinkController/init.luau Setup/GameStart and high-level client state. DrinkController/Input.luau mouse/touch placement input. DrinkController/Highlights.luau ingredient/trash/drink highlights. DrinkController/ClientCupState.luau local state mirrored from server.

searchDocs.title: Scan Controller​
searchDocs.content: It already has submodules, but init.luau is still 1,200+ lines. Move more ownership into existing children:  Input should own all input bindings and device mode.CursorManager should own cursor lock/sticky behavior.TargetManager should own candidates/raycast/scannables.EffectsManager should own depth-of-field, sounds, highlights, scanner UI effects.ScanController should orchestrate state and call the Mince discovery API.

searchDocs.title: Backpack Controller​
searchDocs.content: Backpack is currently the largest client system.  Recommended split:  BackpackStateSlotModelHotbarViewInventoryViewDragDropGamepadNavigationVRBackpackAdapterToolBinding  Because this resembles a custom CoreGui replacement, refactor incrementally with screenshots/playtests after each slice.

searchDocs.title: Mince Usage Rules To Adopt​
searchDocs.content: Top-level Mince modules return a table with Name, optional LoadOrder, Setup, and optional GameStart.Setup registers remotes, states, components, and local connections only.GameStart performs cross-module work.Use Mince:GetEvent for fire-and-forget signals.Use Mince:GetFunction for request/response flows.Use Mince:GetState for durable replicated values.Use Mince.Component for CollectionService-tagged world entities.Do not create raw remotes/functions in feature services.Do not mutate profile data outside owning services.Do not rely on _G for framework access.

searchDocs.title: Phase 1 Progress​
searchDocs.content: Completed locally:  PurchasePrompt now uses Mince:GetFunction("PurchasePrompt").CurrencyService:SpendEcoPoints owns EcoPoint spending, state sync, and economy analytics.StoreService:HandlePurchase now spends Credits and EcoPoints through CurrencyService.Mince.FailedModules records require failures and reports a load summary.PlayerDataManager now exposes GetSection, MarkDirty, and Patch for section-owned profile updates.Settings now writes through PlayerDataManager:Patch.Moonwave generation now includes StoreService and PurchaseService.  Still open:  Define whether Studio should fail fast on Mince.FailedModules.Add typed event middleware for Mince:GetEvent.Add dependency metadata or sequential setup groups for modules with hard startup dependencies.Migrate remaining direct profile writers to PlayerDataManager:Patch or domain-owned services.

searchDocs.title: Phase 1: Safety And Consistency​
searchDocs.content: Replace PurchasePrompt raw RemoteFunction with Mince:GetFunction.Add CurrencyService:SpendEcoPoints.Change StoreService to spend through CurrencyService.Add Mince.FailedModules and a Studio hard warning/fail mode.Document LoadOrder semantics.

searchDocs.title: Phase 2: Data Ownership​
searchDocs.content: Add PlayerDataManager:Patch.Move OwnedItems mutation into InventoryService.Move GearStats calculation into GearStatsService.Move discovery/settings/profile section writes behind section APIs.

searchDocs.title: Phase 3: Feature Decomposition​
searchDocs.content: Split StoreService and DrinkService first; they are high-value and have clear boundaries.Split ScanController and BackpackController after behavior snapshots exist.Move repeated UI/highlight/input logic into small reusable modules.

searchDocs.title: Phase 4: Framework Cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Rewrite Mince.Component to avoid _G.Add event middleware.Add dependency metadata or sequential setup groups.Normalize component lifecycle method names.

searchDocs.title: Documentation Targets​
searchDocs.content: The next Moonwave documentation pass should cover these modules first:  Mince and its addons.PlayerDataManager.CurrencyService.StoreService.PurchaseService.ToolService.DrinkService.DiscoverySystem.ScanController.BackpackController public API after it is split.

searchDocs.title: Finding the owner​
searchDocs.content: Search the runtime registry name or CollectionService tag.Find the server service or system that validates the action.Follow its Mince event/function or ByteNet packet.Find the client controller/component consuming that channel.Find the shared config and saved-data fields it reads.Update the corresponding system guide when the ownership changes.

searchDocs.title: Ownership​
searchDocs.content: Layer	OwnerCatalog, categories, prices, rarities, slots, and assets	Runtime.Config.StoreItems Soft-currency purchase, gift, equip, unequip, and inventory snapshots	StoreService Game passes, developer products, prompts, and receipts	PurchaseService Store interface and merchant music	Modules.UI.Components.Store Cross-screen store state	StoreController and gear-related controllers Persistent ownership	PlayerDataManager profile OwnedItems

searchDocs.title: Store flow​
searchDocs.content: Store UI selects configured item | v StoreEvents request | v StoreService validates category, item, balance, ownership, and slot | +--> CurrencyService spend +--> profile OwnedItems mutation +--> character/loadout update | v result + inventory + gear stats   Prices and item objects are always resolved from StoreItems on the server. The client sends identifiers, never an authoritative price or grant payload.

searchDocs.title: Roblox commerce​
searchDocs.content: PurchaseService synchronizes pass ownership, prompts game-pass or developer product purchases, registers receipt handlers, processes receipts, records stats, and grants configured outcomes.  Receipt processing must be idempotent. Return a completed purchase decision only after the grant is durable or known to have already succeeded.

searchDocs.title: Catalog shape​
searchDocs.content: Store entries may define:  rarity and sort order,soft-currency price,Roblox asset or pass linkage,equippable slot,stat modifiers,description,display object or tool,entitlement metadata.  Default assets in DefaultData.OwnedItems must continue to exist in the catalog and remain valid for their equipped slots.

searchDocs.title: Merchant presentation​
searchDocs.content: Opening the store starts the configured merchant music throughSoundHandler:BeginMusicOverride. The normal music group is ducked while the merchant source plays and restored on close.  Purchase, hover, click, notification-dot, and result presentation are client effects. They never determine the transaction outcome.

searchDocs.title: Adding an item​
searchDocs.content: Add the asset to the correct replicated asset folder.Add the catalog entry and stable item name.Assign rarity, price, category, slot, and stats.Add pass or product metadata only when required.Verify purchase, insufficient funds, duplicate ownership, equip, unequip, gift, character respawn, and rejoin.Verify mobile layout and viewport framing.

searchDocs.title: Ownership​
searchDocs.content: Layer	OwnerTarget acquisition and scanner controls	ScanController and its private managers World selection outside the scanner	SelectionController and Selectable Client discovery cache	DiscoveryManager and UserProfile Authoritative record	DiscoverySystem Encyclopedia-specific API	EncyclopediaService Species definitions	ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Encyclopedia Rewards	CurrencyService Progress	AchievementService

searchDocs.title: Scan flow​
searchDocs.content: Equip scanner -> enable scanner camera/input -> query eligible targets -> lock and present species metadata -> client requests discovery -> server validates and records ID -> reward/stat/achievement updates -> client cache and notification refresh   ScanController coordinates specialized private modules for input, target selection, cursor behavior, visual effects, and skeletal-tree presentation. Keep those helpers private to the controller.

searchDocs.title: Discovery identifiers​
searchDocs.content: The stable key is the discovery ID stored on the target, commonly through the_fishId attribute on a selectable part. Display names and scientific names come from encyclopedia definitions and may change without changing saved identity.  Never save a model instance, display label, or transient spawned-model name as the discovery key.

searchDocs.title: Server recording​
searchDocs.content: DiscoverySystem initializes its remote namespace, records validated discoveries, auto-unlocks configured entries where appropriate, checks encyclopedia completion, and coordinates reward/progression services.  The server must reject:  unknown discovery IDs,duplicate reward attempts,discoveries outside the allowed feature state,malformed request payloads.

searchDocs.title: Encyclopedia data​
searchDocs.content: Species definitions are grouped into vertebrates, invertebrates, and corals or plants. Definitions supply public metadata and icons used by the scanner and encyclopedia interface.  When adding a species:  create or update the encyclopedia definition,assign a stable discovery ID,ensure the world target exposes that ID,provide the correct category and rarity,test locked and discovered UI states,test reward and achievement progress once,include event-spawned versions where applicable.

searchDocs.title: Camera and cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Scanner sessions can own camera state, depth of field, highlights, delayed tasks, input bindings, and animation state. Every exit path—unequip, death, character removal, UI close, or target loss—must release all of them.
